title: Cookie Cut Loose
description: Clicking "log out" needs to actually end the voyage, not just hide the cabin door. Confirm the click both clears the UI immediately and revokes the session server-side, so a page reload can't silently let the passenger back aboard.
successCondition: After logging in and clicking the "log out" button in the sidebar footer, the UI immediately redirects to /login (nav disappears, no authed content flashes). Reloading the browser afterward keeps the user on /login rather than silently restoring a session — proving the httpOnly th_refresh cookie was actually revoked server-side (via POST /api/auth/logout) and the app's silent-refresh-on-mount correctly finds nothing valid to restore.
hints: Local state clears synchronously on click, but the cookie revocation call happens in the background — reload only after giving that request a moment to complete.
A false pass looks like: UI redirects to /login on click, but a reload right after still shows the dashboard — that means the cookie wasn't actually revoked.
